originalTitle: Two Reasons To Stay Away From Carvana Stock
summary: During the second quarter of 2026, Carvana (CVNA) grew its revenue 52% to hit a company record, while also selling 38% more retail cars. Even with this rapid expansion, the stock has lost 15.1% over the past twelve months, significantly trailing the 17.1% return of the S&P 500. Shareholders are finding out that high top-line numbers do not guarantee market rewards. So why would you stay away from a company growing this fast.
content:
During the second quarter of 2026, Carvana (CVNA) grew its revenue 52% to hit a company record, while also selling 38% more retail cars. Even with this rapid expansion, the stock has lost 15.1% over the past twelve months, significantly trailing the 17.1% return of the S&P 500. Shareholders are finding out that high top-line numbers do not guarantee market rewards. So why would you stay away from a company growing this fast?

On Earnings, Carvana Is Priced Above The S&P 500

Valuation provides the first warning sign. Carvana stock trades at 28.7 times earnings , compared to 21.5 for the S&P 500.

Investors are clearly not paying that premium for current profitability. Carvana’s operating margin over the past twelve months was 8.9%, trailing the 18.5% margin recorded by the broader index. The market appears to be pricing in sustained expansion instead. Carvana has averaged annual revenue growth of 30.8% over three years, far outpacing the 5.8% pace set by the S&P 500. Anyone acquiring shares at today’s price is heavily reliant on those growth rates holding steady.

Can Carvana Get Enough Cars Ready To Sell?

The company has struggled to meet its own supply needs so far. During the second-quarter call in July, management identified a notable headwind: inventory had expanded at a slower pace than sales for several months.

However, demand remains solid whenever vehicles actually hit the lot. To clear this bottleneck, Carvana has been expanding its capacity to prepare cars across its ADESA facilities and existing inspection centers. The strategy yielded clear results in the second quarter. Regions with the heaviest capacity investments saw inventory grow 57% and sales grow 54%. By contrast, areas with the lightest upgrades saw inventory grow 17% and sales grew 30%.

Despite that underlying demand, the internal profit outlook is cautious. Management forecast adjusted EBITDA, a profit measure before interest, taxes and depreciation, to land between $2.7 billion and $3.0 billion for 2026. That marks an increase from $2.24 billion last year. Carvana’s second-quarter result was already running at an annual rate above $3 billion. The top end of that range is no higher than the yearly pace Carvana already hit in the second quarter. On the July call, an analyst noted the guidance implies a step down in the second half.

How Much Has Carvana Lost When Stocks Sold Off?

Historical volatility provides a second reason for caution. The stock has underperformed the S&P 500 during three past shocks by a wide margin. When the 2025 tariff shock hit, Carvana stock fell 42%, compared to a 19% decline for the S&P 500. During the 2023 yield shock, shares fell 41% while the index lost 9.5%. The damage was even more severe in the 2022 inflation shock, when Carvana stock lost 94% against a 24% retreat for the broader market.

Given the severity of these drawdowns, the size of your position in Carvana matters a great deal.

What Should You Watch In Carvana’s Next Report?

Moving forward, the critical metric to monitor is the number of cars Carvana sold to retail customers during the third quarter. On the July call, management stated they expected to sell more retail cars in the third quarter than in the second, when the company sold a record 197,325. Independent indicators support this optimism. In late September, Jefferies noted that website data showed Carvana’s vehicle sales growth accelerating to about 40% in recent weeks. Delivering a count clearly above 197,325 would confirm the company is getting cars ready fast enough to keep growing. A count at or below that threshold, however, would fall short of management’s own guidance.

chineseTitle: 远离 Carvana 股票的两个原因
chineseSummary: 2026 年第二季度，Carvana (CVNA) 的收入增长了 52%，创下公司纪录，同时零售汽车销量也增加了 38%。即使如此快速扩张，该股在过去 12 个月内仍下跌了 15.1%，明显落后于标准普尔 500 指数 17.1% 的回报率。股东们发现，高额营收数字并不能保证市场回报。那么，您为什么要远离一家发展如此迅速的公司呢？
chineseContent:
2026 年第二季度，Carvana (CVNA) 的收入增长了 52%，创下公司纪录，同时零售汽车销量也增加了 38%。即使如此快速扩张，该股在过去 12 个月内仍下跌了 15.1%，明显落后于标准普尔 500 指数 17.1% 的回报率。股东们发现，高额营收数字并不能保证市场回报。那么，您为什么要远离一家发展如此迅速的公司呢？

就盈利而言，Carvana 的定价高于标准普尔 500 指数

估值提供了第一个警告信号。 Carvana 股票的市盈率为 28.7 倍，而标准普尔 500 指数的市盈率为 21.5 倍。

投资者显然不会为当前的盈利能力支付如此高的溢价。 Carvana 过去 12 个月的营业利润率为 8.9%，落后于更广泛指数记录的 18.5% 利润率。相反，市场似乎正在考虑持续扩张。 Carvana 三年来平均年收入增长率为 30.8%，远远超过标准普尔 500 指数设定的 5.8% 的增速。任何以今天的价格收购股票的人都严重依赖这些增长率的稳定。

Carvana 能有足够的汽车准备出售吗？

到目前为止，该公司一直在努力满足自己的供应需求。在 7 月份的第二季度电话会议中，管理层发现了一个明显的不利因素：库存增长速度连续几个月低于销售速度。

然而，每当车辆实际到达停车场时，需求仍然强劲。为了克服这一瓶颈，Carvana 一直在扩大其 ADESA 设施和现有检验中心的汽车准备能力。该策略在第二季度取得了明显的成果。产能投资最多的地区库存增长了 57%，销售额增长了 54%。相比之下，升级最少的区域库存增长了 17%，销售额增长了 30%。

尽管存在潜在需求，但内部利润前景仍持谨慎态度。管理层预测，调整后的 EBITDA（利息、税项和折旧前利润指标）到 2026 年将达到 27 亿美元至 30 亿美元之间。这比去年的 22.4 亿美元有所增加。 Carvana 第二季度的业绩已经以年增长率超过 30 亿美元。该范围的上限不高于卡瓦纳在第二季度已经达到的年增长率。在 7 月份的电话会议上，一位分析师指出，该指引意味着下半年将有所下降。

股票抛售时卡瓦纳损失了多少？

历史波动性提供了第二个需要谨慎的理由。在过去的三次冲击中，该股的表现大幅落后于标准普尔 500 指数。当 2025 年关税冲击来袭时，Carvana 股票下跌 42%，而标准普尔 500 指数则下跌 19%。在 2023 年收益率冲击期间，股价下跌 41%，而该指数下跌 9.5%。在 2022 年通胀冲击中，损失更为严重，当时 Carvana 股票下跌 94%，而大盘则下跌 24%。

考虑到这些缩编的严重性，您在 Carvana 的持仓规模非常重要。

Carvana 的下一份报告中您应该关注哪些内容？

展望未来，需要监控的关键指标是第三季度 Carvana 向零售客户销售的汽车数量。在 7 月份的电话会议上，管理层表示，他们预计第三季度的零售汽车销量将超过第二季度，当时该公司售出了创纪录的 197,325 辆汽车。独立指标支持了这种乐观情绪。 9月下旬，杰富瑞指出，网站数据显示Carvana的汽车销量增长在最近几周加速至40%左右。数量明显高于 197,325 辆将证实该公司正在以足够快的速度准备汽车以保持增长。然而，等于或低于该阈值的计数将达不到管理层自己的指导。

现在您对 CVNA 有了更多的了解。这就是我们的目的：让您在投资之前了解情况。然而，押注单一股票有其自身的风险。
